messages.subject: Questions Regarding my Modeling Strategy
parts:
Hi All:

I am currently working on a Distance Sampling modeling project as part of
my MS work and had a couple questions:

-Is the "shotgun approach" of looking at all possible model combinations
better, or are there model combinations that are better suited for line
transects (which is how my data was collected?



-I have been adding three series expansions at a time for each analysis. Are
these each analyzed separately or do each of them additively alter the
result?



Ex. If I do a Half Normal model of MAWR (Marsh Wren) and select all three
series expansions when I am defining the model would this be three separate
models (HN + Cos, HN + Hermite Polynomial, HN + Simple Polynomial) or would
it be one model (HN + Cos + HP + SP)?

Thanks for reading!

Cheers,
Ben Wishnek

messages.subject: Re: Questions Regarding my Modeling Strategy
parts:
Ben:

The short answer to your question is to not use the shotgun approach of
all possible model. If you have a copy of Buckland et al. (2001) at
your disposal, have a look at section 2.4 for a discussion of natural
pairings of key functions and adjustment terms.

The answer to your second question is that you could fit 3 different
models: half-normal key with cosine adjustment, half-normal key with
Hermite adjustment, half-normal key with simple polynomial adjustment.
